title: Atypical cells in urine - Validation of a new tumormarker in urothelial carcinoma (AG ACU)
summary:
The main goal of this study is to see if a new test can help diagnose urothelial carcinoma (a type of bladder cancer) by looking for "atypical cells" in urine.

To do this, researchers will analyze urine samples using a special machine called the Sysmex UF-5000. The machine helps sort the cells in the urine by looking at their size and genetic material. This process helps identify "atypical cells," which are unusual cells that often come from bladder cancer and could suggest the presence of the disease.

For the study, urine samples will be collected from two different groups of people, likely one group with bladder cancer and another without, to test how well this method works.
